Issue 375 is fixed in one commit, 914ce4cc, on branch fix/375-openrouter-base-url-on-every-route in /tmp/wt-375. Its parent is 402a8013. It is not pushed.

The bug: only the launch applied OPENROUTER_BASE_URL. Every model copy the registry handed out kept providers.openrouter.baseUrl from models.json, or https://openrouter.ai/api/v1. So after a /model pick of an OpenRouter model, the prompt and the user's OpenRouter key went to openrouter.ai or to the models.json host, not to the user's gateway.

The fix: one function now owns the variable, model_registry.with_openrouter_base_url(model). It acts only when the provider is exactly 'openrouter' and the value is set and not empty. It changes base_url and no other field.
- ModelRegistry hands every model out through a new _served_models(). get_all, get_available and find read through it, and compose_built_in's composition branch applies the function too.
- The value is read when a model is handed out, not when models.json loads. A registry built before a hatched .env value arrived therefore still agrees with the launch.
- Copies are cached per (load, value), so a model's identity is stable between reads.
- The launch's runtime_bootstrap._openrouter_base now calls the same function. It still covers a launch with no registry, a duck-typed registry and a backfill.

Precedence is the launch's since issue 344: the variable beats a per-model baseUrl in models.json, then providers.openrouter.baseUrl, then the catalog host. No other provider is ever re-pointed, including a gateway the user named something else that serves the same ids. What a .env may set is unchanged: the variable still comes from the shell, or from a .env only when AELIX_DOTENV_ALLOW names it.

pi (27c7b6ff4) has no OPENROUTER_BASE_URL. Its only override is providers.openrouter.baseUrl, which it applies to every model it composes (provider-composer.ts:326-329). This change applies aelix's variable the same way.

#354 implement.summary:
Fixed #354 in one commit, 46c63ba2 on fix/354-delegated-child-inherits-thinking in /tmp/wt-354, based on 402a8013. Not pushed.

What changed: a delegated child whose profile has no thinking: setting now starts with --thinking set to the parent's effective level. The level is read once per spawn and takes the same late-bound path as the model (#304, ADR-0243 section 9):
- cli/entry.py passes AgentsExtension(thinking=lambda: _live_thinking_of(session_host)), which reads runtime.harness.state.thinking_level.
- AgentsExtension._host_thinking asks that getter first, then the live ExtensionAPI.get_thinking_level. There is no _ctx fallback because ExtensionContext has no thinking level.
- SubagentHost.thinking feeds runtime._parent_thinking. That read is guarded: a getter that raises, a non-string, or a value outside VALID_THINKING_LEVELS counts as no evidence, and the child gets no flag (the argv it had before).
- The value goes into SpawnPlan.parent_thinking. A new print_channel.inherit_thinking runs in both the print and rpc channels, next to narrow_context_files. So resolver.profile_to_flags is still the only place --thinking is emitted, and it never appears twice.

Precedence: the profile's own thinking: wins, whatever model the profile names. Next comes the parent's level. Otherwise nothing is emitted.

What effective means per mode:
- TUI: the defaultThinkingLevel seed, or whatever /thinking set since.
- -p, --mode json, --mode rpc: --thinking or an --agent profile's thinking:, otherwise off. These modes still do not apply defaultThinkingLevel (#286, not touched). So a headless parent with no --thinking now passes --thinking off. The wire is the same as before for both parent and child: reasoning effort none (measured).

What pi does: its subagent example (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts, commit e3798ca91, pi #7897) pushes --thinking ctx.thinkingLevel only when the agent file names no model, together with the inherited model. pi agent files have no thinking field. We followed the decision as given and inherit regardless of the profile's model. The divergence is recorded in the ADR and listed under owner decisions.

The #389 fix is one commit on branch fix/389-bash-approval-shows-the-whole-command in /tmp/wt-389, on top of 402a8013. It is not pushed.

Before changing anything I reproduced the defect on 402a8013 with my own pty driver (real CLI, 80x24, scripted mock model). The bash command "true arg000 .. arg399 ; echo TAIL_MARKER_389 >> out.txt" showed only up to arg130, and pressing 1 ran it. I found two more cases the issue did not list. A 121-line write and an edit were applied on 1, because their preview stops at 40 lines (_MAX_BODY_LINES). A write of one 265-character line fit on screen, but its end was cut with an ellipsis at the box width (_render_diff caps the width). In all four runs the tail was never on screen.

What changed (packages/aelix-coding-agent/src/aelix_coding_agent/tui/approval_dialog.py):
1. Every approval kind (bash, write, edit, other) now draws its body through one viewport, _BodyViewport. This is #188's _ArgumentViewport renamed, not a parallel copy. Yes, "Yes, for this session" and any other approving row wait until every body line has been drawn by a real paint. No, Esc and Ctrl+C always answer. When the body overflows, the row above the options names the hidden line count, PgUp/PgDn, and "Yes held until all seen". ADR-0159's cursor-following body is removed.
2. Nothing in an approval is elided any more. The write/edit diff is rendered with every line and no width cap, so long rows wrap, and _MAX_BODY_LINES is gone. The 200-character cut on each argument value of tools aelix did not build stays; ADR-0253 section 8 decided it and it shows a marker.
3. I found a related bypass and fixed it here. ESC [8m inside a command hid the rest of that line while the dialog counted it as drawn, and \x01..\x02 was written to the terminal raw (measured on 402a8013). Every model- or author-chosen string in the body and title now goes through safe_for_terminal; the literal "[8m" stays visible.
4. PgUp/PgDn now move one screen less one line instead of 5 lines. No line is skipped, and the 121-line write takes 9 presses at 80x24 instead of 25.
5. The footer switches to a short form when the full sentence is wider than the modal, so "Yes held" is never the part that gets cut off.
6. builtin/permission.py: the ctx.ui.select fallback title now carries the whole bash command or write path. It used to stop at 120 characters.

pi check (rule 11, /tmp/pi-27c7b6ff4): pi has no permission gate. Its examples/extensions/permission-gate.ts puts the whole command into a ctx.ui.select title. ExtensionSelectorComponent draws that title as wrapped Text with no height cap, in the terminal's own scrollback, and never checks that it was read. aelix diverges because its modal is height-capped (ADR-0159), which is why it needs the viewport and the hold. This is recorded in ADR-0253 section 11.

I fixed #392 in one commit, b9314a0a, on fix/392-catalog-install-ignores-cwd-uv-config in /tmp/wt-392 (parent 402a8013, main has not moved, not pushed).

The fix follows owner option a. `aelix extension discover install` (every entry form) and every `aelix extension update` now run the installer in `<agent dir>/installer-cwd` instead of the current directory. That covers uv and pip, and also the `pip download` of the verify step. The new `catalog_installer_cwd()` creates the directory with mode 0700 and writes one `uv.toml` into it. That file contains only comments, so it sets nothing. Because uv reads only the nearest project config, that file stops uv from looking any further up. Nothing in the cwd, its parents or above the agent dir is read, including `~/uv.toml` and `~/pyproject.toml`.

What still applies: the user-level `uv.toml`, the system one (via XDG_CONFIG_DIRS), `UV_CONFIG_FILE` and `UV_*`, so the ADR-0200 org index pin keeps working. If the directory cannot be created, the install is refused with exit 2; it never falls back to the cwd. The consent block names the directory.

`_uv_config_files` now returns only the nearest project config, as uv itself reads it, asked from the directory uv runs in. The `cwd` is passed through uv_ambient_index_env, uv_ambient_index_config and _uv_has_own_index_config. This closes ADR-0200 section 9 item 3: before, a `[tool.uv]` index in a file uv never read could switch off the pip.conf translation and lose the org pin.

A relative `--index-url ./simple` typed on `discover install` is turned into an absolute path from the cwd first. uv would otherwise read it from its own working directory; pip refuses relative index paths.

Update decision: install records do not say whether a catalog chose their source (they hold only spec, kind and name). So every `update` runs in the installer directory, including records from typed installs and `update <unrecorded name>`. Every recorded spec is absolute by the time it reaches the installer, and a relative `git+file:./x` installs on neither backend (measured).

The pip backend also runs there, for a measured reason: `python -m pip` puts its working directory first on sys.path, and a `pip/` package in the cwd ran as the installer.

A typed `aelix extension install` still runs in the cwd. This is written down as a known limit in ADR-0255 section 12, the guide and the CHANGELOG.

What pi does: it runs `npm install <spec> --prefix <agentDir>/npm` with no cwd. npm 11.19.0 reads the `.npmrc` in the --prefix root, not the cwd's (measured), so a project `.npmrc` cannot redirect a pi user-scope install. This change does the same thing for aelix.

Docs changed: ADR-0255 (status line, section 12 rewritten, new section 15 with measurements, sweep, pi and limits), ADR-0200 (status line, section 9 item 3, new section 12), decisions/README rows 0200 and 0255, docs/guides/private-catalog.md and the bundled copy, CHANGELOG Security (new #392 entry; the #131 entry's 'left to a follow-up' now points to it). findings.title: Cat 2: docs say a parent with no --thinking passes off, which is too broad
findings.detail: The new guide (docs/guides/agent-profiles.md:120), the CHANGELOG, the ADR amendment and the source docstrings say that a headless parent run without --thinking passes 'off' to the child. That is false in general. Delegation reads the live harness state, and that state can also come from the parent profile's thinking: frontmatter, from a restored session, or from a /thinking change made later. Only a fresh headless parent with nothing else set passes off today (#286 is unchanged). Suggested rewording: delegation reads the live harness state; the TUI seeds defaultThinkingLevel when nothing else set it; the CLI flag, the profile, a restored session and /thinking can each set it; a fresh, otherwise-unset headless parent passes off.
